method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across the quality of welcome and fellowship across divisions, prayer, music and the preparation of worship, hospitality, shared tables and the Nineteen Day Feast, consultation, learning and practical care, communities remembered and visited, wisdom and fellowship amid danger, nearness across distance and prayers for those gathered, and later guidance on devotional meetings and convention consultation. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. Imported wording checked separately; version differences remain explicit. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing friends chanting with a new song in love and supplication, and crying, “O how we miss you!”; an intimate expression of remembrance across distance.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words answering why one should pray with others when one can pray alone: when many gather their force is greater, like a united army rather than separate soldiers.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising the steadfast meetings of the friends in Yazd and foreseeing that, if continued, they will influence East and West.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaching that Bahá’u’lláh has so united hearts that they correspond without pen and paper.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words at the same London Feast to spread the feast and give refreshments, assuring material and spiritual benefits and the breath of the Holy Spirit.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping the friends will remain united in utmost wisdom and kindle one another’s joy and fervour through the mention of the Ancient Beauty.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá rejoicing in praise of the Parsee assembly as a spiritual gathering reflecting the pattern of the supreme gatherings.

selected.text: O Lord! selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking God to illumine the gatherings of the friends, perfume their meeting places and gladden their ears with the call of the Concourse on High.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá naming the mention of God, teaching and the exposition of the teachings as the candle of the gathering, which then becomes heavenly and a cause of guidance.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explaining that although gatherings reflect the Concourse on High, the enmity of opponents requires tact and meetings of no more than nineteen.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words urging study in meetings and homes and warning against idle discussion of problems that bear no result.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on a house prepared for Him in New York, asking that unity and harmony make it so full of light that all feel He is present.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s recollection of ten people living in one small room on a few dates who chanted and sang till past midnight, forgetting their outward circumstances; a narrative of spiritual fellowship in poverty.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling a gathering of children in Esslingen whose sweetness He still remembers; a narrative of children in community life.

selected.text: The gatherings that thou dost arrange in thine own home are a source of strength to the hearts of the spiritually-minded, of guidance to the seekers, and of awakening to those who slumber. selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing home gatherings as a source of strength to the spiritually minded, guidance to seekers and awakening to those who slumber.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s recollection of His spiritual gatherings in America and Europe, including a Washington meeting so effective that the Turkish Ambassador wept.

selected.text: They envision that on specified days they will form an assembly in that gathering and consult, and adhere to and pursue whatever causes the spread of the light of guidance. selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on friends who resolve to meet on specified days to consult and pursue whatever spreads guidance, calling such an assembly a rose garden if its conditions are fulfilled.

selected.text: O Muhammad! Blessed is the house wherein are diffused the fragrances of Revelation and wherein is raised the remembrance of God, the Mighty, the All-Knowing, the Wise.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh calling the house where the loved ones raise their call and remember God the circling-place of the near angels.

No station equalleth this station
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh praising a believer who traversed prairies, deserts, seas and mountains on the wings of yearning to reach His presence; carries journeys toward the gathering.

selected.text: I am leaving Paris for the Orient though in reality I am always with you. Place does not matter. Two people may be in the same room and yet not attain to a visitation. selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words on leaving Paris that place does not matter: two in one room may not truly meet, while some in distant lands attain the meeting; the guide’s key teaching on nearness.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling for a study class for teaching and for gatherings in which conversation turns to proofs so the friends may become proficient.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words advising a committee to superintend the feasts and keep a record as friends offer to host them; a distinctive practical arrangement.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing the hearts of the friends as mirrors in which each countenance is reflected in another’s heart, so that embracing one another they demonstrate oneness.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words asking that a departed believer’s anniversary be marked by visiting his tomb and, if possible, spreading a feast for the poor and giving charity; turns remembrance into care.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words to a Russian princess hoping that, though they may never meet again in the body, their spirits may commune on the plane of Reality.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá directing that a house be quietly used for gatherings of dawn prayer, with utmost caution in Shiraz so that strangers never learn of it.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising Naw-Rúz hospitality that prepares both heavenly sustenance and physical food so that guests may read, discuss, speak and listen.

selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing a festival of affection, chanting and teaching, arranged through spiritual sentiments, as a “Lord’s Supper” that causes everlasting life.

selected.text: Bad conduct or deeds are not allowed at any time and especially during the Feast. But those are the days of happiness, days of joy and gladness. This is from the verses that shall be known afterwards. For example, it is bad not to work on other days, but in these days of feasts, work must be abandoned. But it does not mean that it is permissible to drink liquor or commit immoral deeds. Those days are the days of forgiveness and pardon, days of cheer and enjoyment, days of affection and attraction, days of blessings
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words that feast days are days of joy, forgiveness and abandoning work, but never licence for liquor or immoral deeds; a necessary qualification on celebration.

selected.text: However, since it contained the glad tidings of the fellowship of the friends and establishment of a gathering of the beloved ones, it brought the utmost joy and delight - provided that it proves lasting and does not endure for just a few days, after which weariness sets in and darkness appears in hearts, causing the dispersal of the gathering and the scattering of the assembly.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá rejoicing in a new gathering provided it proves lasting, and not one that disperses after a few days when weariness sets in; an honest qualification.

selected.text: O friends! To chant the verses of Divine Unity with a soul-stirring melody by night and by day is the exclusive privilege of the people of God. selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling the chanting of the verses of divine unity with soul-stirring melody, by night and day, the special privilege of the people of God.

selected.text: The gathering you have arranged in your home is a heavenly gathering, for the Sun of Truth has cast its rays upon it. In that gathering the mention of God is spread abroad, hearts are turned toward the divine Kingdom, and eyes are opened to witness the signs of the All-Merciful. Persist in holding this gathering and strive day by day to strengthen its foundations and organize its affairs.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling a home gathering heavenly and asking the host to persist and strengthen its foundations day by day.

selected.text: With regard to the assembly, there must be spiritual consultation therein; discourses about the manifestation of the Greatest Orb, the effulgence of the Sun of Reality, the greatness of the blessed Cause, the power and penetration of the Word of God, the might of the divine Covenant and Testament must be mentioned. This will be conducive to the spirituality and illumination of the hearts.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking for spiritual consultation in the assembly on the greatness of the Cause and the power of the Word and the Covenant.

selected.text: Therefore, you must manifest in gatherings of the loved ones and meetings of the chosen ones an eloquent tongue, a brilliant proof, evident attraction, fluent speech and elevated utterance. You must certainly recite verses, prayers and poems in every gathering and deliver speeches with utmost eloquence so that all present may be filled with joy and gladness and all hearts may be attracted.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá urging eloquent speech, verses, prayers and poems in every gathering so that all present may be filled with joy and hearts attracted.

selected.text: O God! Grant that this palace reach completion, and this divinely-ordained temple become a mighty edifice, in order that the melodies of glorification and praise may reach unto the Kingdom, the nightingale's dawn-tide melodies may rise from the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar to the world of mysteries, and the Concourse on High and the inmates of the Kingdom of Glory may be filled with joy and gladness.
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking that the temple be completed so that melodies of praise may rise from the Mashriqu’l-Adhkár to the Kingdom.

selected.text: How spiritual are our meetings! In the utmost love are we set aglow! The hearts are all attracted to each other. It is just like being one soul, one body. Such a meeting as this is impossible and cannot be organized save through the Love of God. There is no material interest whatsoever. There is no worldly desire at all. In the utmost purity and holiness has the Force of Divinity assembled us.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words that such a meeting, free of material interest and worldly desire, is like one soul and one body and cannot be organized save through the love of God.

selected.text: spiritual friends! Your letter describing the Ridvan feast and spiritual gathering was read with utmost joy. Praise be to God that there was an assembly there in complete attraction who are turned toward the Abha Kingdom and desire to sacrifice their lives in the path of God. Therefore, 'Abdu'l-Baha has the utmost hope in those blessed souls that in a short time they will become the cause of the spread of the divine fragrances. However, with wisdom, they should always arrange feasts on the appointed days and hold heavenly gatherings and engage in the mention
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising a Ridván feast and asking that, with wisdom, feasts always be held on the appointed days; joins hospitality with sacred times.

selected.text: But now beneath the Bounty and Favor of the Blessed Perfection - - May my life be a sacrifice to his believers! - - such great meetings of different nationalities and religions are held here at the foot of Mount Carmel, adjoining the Tomb of the Blessed Herald of the Day of God, Tablets were chanted, poems are recited, speeches are delivered and the feasts of marriages between the friends are held
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words rejoicing that great meetings of different nationalities and religions are now held at the foot of Mount Carmel, with Tablets chanted, speeches delivered and marriage feasts held.

selected.text: The greater their purity, the greater their reflected splendour. … Wherefore, let us arise, let us bestir ourselves, let us rally round the Standard of the One True God, and gather together under the shadow of the Lord's Sacred Tree, the Tree that hath voiced the Call of God and uttered the Word of Truth. This is indeed, in the eyes of the Lord, your God, the Gracious, a supreme and glorious triumph
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Although our assembly tonight numbers only ten outwardly, in reality it is representative of all the beloved of God.  Why?  Because it pictures the Baha'i community.  The seed, no matter how small, in the estimation of the perceptive mind, is a veritable tree.  The mind images the tree and the tree is revealed from the seed.  Likewise, when I see you it is as though I were seeing all the beloved of God
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words that an assembly of only ten represents all the beloved of God, as the perceptive mind sees the tree within the seed; a memorable answer to concern about small numbers.

selected.text: Praise be to God that the lights of the Sun of Reality show forth from the horizon of Urbana and the Mysteries of the Kingdom became manifest. What a merciful assembly is founded! What a lordly circle is organized! This is no other save the confirmations of the Kingdom of Abha; for in that city such a meeting is established! This is the first cornerstone of the divine structure laid in that district.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá greeting the founding of an assembly in Urbana as the first cornerstone of the divine structure in that district.

selected.text: Give the utmost importance to the Nineteen-day Feasts, so that the Friends of God and the Maidservants of the Merciful may turn their faces to the Kingdom, read the supplications, entreat for confirmation, be attracted with love for one another, add to their holiness, virtue and sanctity, resist the army of passion and desire, be abstracted from the elemental world and submerged in the sea of spiritual emotions
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking that utmost importance be given to the Nineteen Day Feasts so the friends may turn to the Kingdom, love one another and grow in holiness.

selected.text: Numerous meetings are held in Paris every day for different purposes, to discuss politics, commerce, education, art, science and many other subjects. … All these meetings are good: but this assembly has met together to turn their faces towards God, to learn how best to work for the good of humanity, to seek how prejudices may be abolished, and the seed of love and universal brotherhood sown in the heart of man
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: upon the Abha Kingdom! In these days when the Lamp of the Covenant is burning brightly in all regions and the lights of the bounties of the Most Great Luminary are illumining East and West from the Kingdom of the Unseen, making them the envy of the world, the divine foundation must be laid upon humility and lowliness
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that in these days the divine foundation must be laid upon humility and lowliness; carries the guide’s theme of humility.

selected.text: Meetings organized with the utmost holiness and piety, wherein those who are present engage in the mention and thought of God, and wherein the verses of Oneness are chanted and the prayers of the Threshold of the Lord of Verses are offered and the exhortations and counsels of the Blessed Beauty recited, such meetings are illumined, spiritual, divine and heavenly. They are the means of training the world of humanity.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing meetings of holiness and piety, with verses, prayers and counsels of the Blessed Beauty, as the means of training the world of humanity.

selected.text: The friends in every land should gather together with wisdom and utterance in meetings and assemblies to read the verses of God, for the verses kindle the fire of love and ignite its flame. However, they must observe wisdom in all conditions, and gatherings of five to nine persons are sufficient. The locations must also be varied, for if they are held in one place, the heedless will become aware and cause commotion.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh bidding the friends gather with wisdom to read the verses, in groups of five to nine and in varied locations, lest the heedless cause commotion.

selected.text: O thou who art attracted to the Covenant! Praise be to God that thou hast made thy home a nest and shelter for the birds of the meadow, transformed it into a rose-garden of oneness, and established it as a gathering place for those who are detached, so that at dawn and daybreak it may become a Mashriqu'l-Adhkar where lights will shine forth and the melody of prayer and supplication will be raised to the Abha Kingdom.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising a believer who made her home a gathering place so that at dawn it might become a Mashriqu’l-Adhkár of prayer and supplication.

selected.text: The Mashriqu'l-Adhkar is the dawning-place of lights and the gathering place of the righteous. Whenever a company of noble souls assemble in a heavenly gathering there and offer supplications, intone divine verses, and chant prayers with wondrous melodies, the inmates of the Concourse on high hearken and call out, crying, "Happy are we; let all the world rejoice!" for, praise be unto God, souls from among the angels of the Kingdom of Glory have arisen in the nether world to commune with their Lord and intone the verses of Divine Unity
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: These gatherings cause the divine table to descend from Heaven, and draw down the confirmations of the All-Merciful. My hope is that the breathings of the Holy Spirit will be wafted over them, and that each one present shall, in great assemblies, with an eloquent tongue and a heart flooded with the love of God, set himself to acclaiming the rise of the Sun of Truth, the dawn of the Day-Star that lighteth all the World.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Every meeting which is held for the purpose of teaching the Cause of God and the people are gathered there to listen to the explanation of the Word and strive to live and act in accord with the advice and exhortation of the Blessed Perfection - that meeting is heavenly and its Cup-bearer is His Holiness Baha'u'llah. The lights of that meeting are the Confirmations of the Kingdom. Time and place have no control over this.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words that every meeting for teaching where people strive to live by the counsels of Bahá’u’lláh is heavenly, its Cup-bearer Bahá’u’lláh, beyond the control of time and place.

selected.text: Regarding arrangements for the Bahai Sunday meeting for the purpose of worship, this is very suitable. But, in a meeting for worship, first, prayer should be chanted and supplication made until all gather; then communion should be made. After praying, sacred readings with melodious voices should be read by all together
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on the Sunday meeting for worship, with prayer chanted until all gather, then communion and sacred readings in melodious voices.

selected.text: The greatest meeting held during the day of Christ was the Lord's supper. There were only twelve. The meeting was held in a very humble quarter with no table, no chairs and no rugs. They sat around a simple wooden board and spoke on the glad tidings of the Kingdom. Now consider the results of that one Supper. One end of Christ's table is in the East, the other is in the West and many nations and tongues are sitting around it
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words that the Lord’s Supper of only twelve, held in a humble quarter around a simple board, now has a table reaching from East to West; the guide’s strongest image of a simple meal.

selected.text: That blessed assemblage was blessed indeed, and 'Abdu'l-Baha was present in spirit, as an intimate companion. On such blessed days, the friends of God must renew their unity and oneness, and must associate with one another in perfect love and kindness, in joy and delight. They must adorn their gathering with the remembrance of God and raise such melody and song as to bring the dwellers of the Kingdom into rapture and ecstasy.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking that on blessed days the friends renew their unity, associate in perfect love and adorn their gathering with remembrance and song.

selected.text: This is a great day - greater than you can comprehend - and you ought to appreciate it. Truly the East and the West now meet together - Persia and America. In the time of Christ the disciples met with Him - it was then also the meeting of the East and West - and their meeting made this one possible, but this meeting is far greater on account of the greater love and unity. Their meeting was the seed and this meeting is the fruits.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words that the meeting of Persia and America is a meeting of East and West, the fruit of which the disciples’ meeting with Christ was the seed.

selected.text: The beloved of God must therefore consider this Day highly blessed, and glorify and praise it greatly. They must bring this Day to a close with the utmost joy and happiness and gather together in the spirit of infinite love and affection. If a sad feeling should have existed between two individuals, it should be cast away with the dawn of this Day: Great joy and happiness must be the common bond of all who come together at this feast.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words that on a holy day any sad feeling between two individuals should be cast away and great joy be the common bond of all who come together at the feast; carries the work of reconciliation.

selected.text: But, praise be to God in Hamadan the merciful assembly is organized. That assembly must be illumined. The illumination of every assembly is teaching the Cause of God. The spiritually of every meeting is the diffusion of the Fragrance of God. The mercifulness of every gathering-place is to correspond the deeds, actions and behaviour in accord with the Teachings
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaching that the illumination of an assembly is teaching and its mercifulness is deeds that accord with the Teachings.

selected.text: The feast (supper) [every nineteen days] is very acceptable and will finally produce good results. The beloved and the maid-servants of the Merciful must inaugurate the feast in such wise as to resurrect the feast of the ancients--namely, the "lord's supper." The attracted maid-servant of God, Mrs..., I hope will be inspired so she may become the means of unity among the friends in every city. That meeting for feast for which thou wert preparing and providing, should recur every so often, so that it may prove a means of attracting the confirmation of the Kingdom of ABHA
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling the nineteen-day feast acceptable and asking that it resurrect the feast of the ancients, the Lord’s Supper, and recur as a means of attracting confirmation; a key comparison for the guide’s question.

selected.text: O thou almighty God! Make the spiritual assembly of Philadelphia the manifestor of invisible confirmations, and the dawning-place of the lights of the Merciful so that its members arise to serve the world of man and be benevolent to the children of humanity, and adore existence and become the cause of Eternal Life. O Lord, make that gathering-place the emblem of the Supreme Concourse, and that congregation the manifest sign of the Supreme Realm.
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá for the Spiritual Assembly of Philadelphia, that its members arise to serve the world of man and be benevolent to humanity; closes with service.

selected.text: As to thy question regarding the meeting of trinity, it is incumbent on thee to make it a meeting of unity, an exposition of the mysteries of singleness, the elevation of the standard of universal love, the spreading of the knowledge of thy Merciful Lord, the guidance of the souls unto the path of the Kingdom of God, the animation of the hearts by the spirit of the love of God, and the purification of the eyes by the light of the knowledge of God
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá answering a question about a “meeting of trinity” by asking that it be made a meeting of unity, universal love and the guidance of souls.

selected.text: Indeed, if an assembly - that is to say, a gathering - of blessed, knowledgeable, and well-informed souls is established where anyone who develops a doubt or uncertainty can receive from that illumined gathering a sufficient and satisfactory explanation to remove such doubts, and which also engages in exhortation and counsel so as to awaken heedless hearts and cause proud souls to become humble and submissive, this would be most fitting and appropriate.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá commending a gathering of knowledgeable souls where anyone with doubts can receive a satisfactory explanation and proud souls become humble; supports honest inquiry.

selected.text: Thou Almighty God! Confirm Thou these friends and the maid-servants of the Merciful! Grant Thou to them assistance. Open Thou before their faces the closed doors and make them intimate with the fragrances of holiness, so that they may become the confident friends of each other; raise the melody and the song of joy and sing the harmony of heaven, in order that they may exhilarate and gladden the regions of the West and impart attraction and ecstasy
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking God to open closed doors before the friends so they may become confident friends of each other and gladden the West.

selected.text: The feast given by the maidservant of God Dr. Moody truly became the cause of joy to the hearts of the maidservants of the All-Merciful and the means of enkindlement of souls. However, the gathering of such an assemblage in one place is causing anxiety in the minds of some of the authorities … The gathering of a large crowd, whether women or men, in one place and the rising of songs and melodies from the women causes agitation in the hearts of the enemies
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising Dr. Moody’s feast while warning that large crowds and the songs of women in one place caused anxiety among the authorities.

selected.text: With perfect wisdom, whenever possible, a gathering of remembrance and devotion should be arranged and the verses of divine unity should be chanted, so that the taste buds of the Concourse on High may be delighted and the hearts of the people of the Most Glorious Kingdom may be gladdened and rejoiced
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá advising that, with perfect wisdom and whenever possible, a gathering of remembrance be arranged and the verses of divine unity chanted.

selected.text: You had given news of the gathering of the friends during the month of Ramadan and their engagement in the remembrance of God. This news had a pleasant effect, for praise be to God, those bewildered by the countenance of the Most Glorious Beloved are in rapture and attraction, and those yearning for the Supreme Kingdom are in joy and expansion. Every gathering in which the remembrance of the Beauty of the All-Merciful occurs - its sweet fragrances perfume the nostrils.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on news of friends gathered in remembrance of God during Ramadan, affirming that every gathering where the All-Merciful is remembered perfumes the nostrils.

selected.text: Thou hast written about the luminous assembly of Washington. It is the cause of rejoicing, as that assembly is the rose garden of divine mysteries and the most sweet fragrances are wafting therefrom. My prayer is that the friends and maidservants of the Merciful on that assembly may persevere with purity of heart and seek to grow day by day. With every passing moment let them become more luminous, and let the members of that assembly make extraordinary progress at the divine threshold.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praying that the friends of the Washington assembly persevere in purity of heart and grow more luminous day by day.

selected.text: In any case, your letter of the 11th of Shawwal [1337] was received. The feast you arranged where the friends of the All-Merciful gathered in fellowship, chanted the clear verses, and became attracted to the Abha Kingdom--that gathering was, in the words of Christ, the Lord's Supper, meaning a heavenly feast and celestial table "wherein is whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling a feast of fellowship and chanting, in the words of Christ, the Lord’s Supper, meaning a heavenly feast and celestial table.

selected.text: Glory be to God! Until when will they turn away and object and say what they do not understand and speak of what they do not comprehend? The cause and reason for these matters in the first instance was the lack of observance of wisdom. His Holiness the Wronged One, meaning the Name of God - upon him be all glory most glorious - in correspondence sent to this servant has greatly complained about the unwisdom shown in the Land of Ta. In one letter he wrote that "this servant was invited to a place, but upon arrival it was observed that fifty or sixty of the friends were gathered. I said: 'Have you not heard of wisdom, that it has been ordained that gatherings should not exceed nine persons?' Similarly, other
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh lamenting the lack of wisdom in the Land of Ta, where fifty or sixty gathered though gatherings were not to exceed nine persons; context for the guide’s restrictions on numbers.

selected.text: O My Name! O thou who travels throughout the lands for My Cause and the exaltation of My Word! Blessed are the houses that become gathering places for the loved ones of God, attracting souls and being adorned by the presence of His chosen ones. Blessed is the land that has attained in My days, which God has made a dwelling place for My pure ones, and blessed is the house that has found the fragrance of My loved ones, and blessed are the faces that have been illumined by the Sun of My loving-kindness.
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh blessing the houses that become gathering places for the loved ones of God, attracting souls and adorned by His chosen ones.

selected.text: According to what is heard and is evident, you have arranged an assembly in the utmost beauty and a number of you present yourselves in that meeting with all love and unity and engage in communion (i.e., reading of the communes), chanting of the verses, spiritual conversation and utterance of the Kingdom. Blessed are ye for having adorned such a meeting and for having prepared such a feast! That gathering receiveth bounty from the Supreme Concourse and that nucleus is under the protection of the Bounty of ABHA.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá blessing a meeting of communion, chanting and spiritual conversation as a nucleus under the protection of the Abhá bounty.

selected.text: the last days of his life His Holiness Christ held one meeting for the apostles; for all of them sat around the same table. From that time it has been called the Lord's supper, because they discussed subjects pertaining to the Kingdom of God. Therefore if a meeting is held, the general discussion of which is spiritual, undoubtedly that meeting is godlike. Strive day and night that your assemblage may become radiant and the hearts illumined. Consort with each other so that your spirits may be stirred into cheerfulness through the Glad-tidings of the Kingdom. If these conditions are
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words explaining that Christ’s last meeting with the apostles is called the Lord’s Supper because they discussed the Kingdom, so any meeting with spiritual discussion is godlike.

selected.text: Think of the meetings in Lake Mohonk Conference, Church of the ascension, Philadelphia Baptist, New York Peace Society, meeting in the building of the Daughters of American Revolution, the public Library, in the Universalist Church in Washington, meetings in the churches and hotels of Chicago, meetings in the Jewish Synagogues, large, public meetings everywhere, and above all think of the farewell heavenly Banquets in Cincinati, Washington and New York! Nothing in the world can equal them in spirituality and grandeur.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s recollection of meetings at Lake Mohonk, churches, synagogues, libraries and banquets across America; the breadth of His public gatherings.

selected.text: You have written concerning the spiritual meetings. … The foundation of the spiritual meetings must be the teaching and delivering of the Cause of God. In these meetings the believers and maid-servants of the Merciful must proclaim the proofs and arguments and explain the signs of the appearance of the Beauty of Abha-May my life by a sacrifice to the beloved ones! Meanwhile they may read some Tablets and Communes, and at the end of the meetings, if they desire to sing with the utmost supplication and meekness, it is acceptable
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words to Mrs Goodall and Mrs Cooper that spiritual meetings rest on teaching, with Tablets and communes, and singing at the end if desired with supplication and meekness.

selected.text: In gatherings that are convened, external conversations should not take place at all. Rather, conversation should be confined to the chanting of verses, the reading of words, and matters pertaining to the Cause of God, such as the exposition of proofs and arguments, clear and evident reasons, and the traces of the Beloved of the worlds. Those who attend such gatherings should, before entering, be adorned with the utmost cleanliness and, turning their attention to the Abha Kingdom, enter in complete humility and submissiveness.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá directing that external conversation be excluded from gatherings, that discussion keep to verses and the Cause of God, and that those attending enter clean and in complete humility.

selected.text: Gather once a week in a public meeting. Before the meeting opens, one must read a prayer or supplication from Baha'u'llah. Afterward they may sing together an anthem or a song. This is optional. They may do it or not. According to their tastes. Then some one may give an address, on some Baha'i subjects. Then they may read Tablets or extracts from the writings of Baha'u'llah such as the hidden words, Tarazat etc. or the news or letters received from other Baha'i Centers. Then with another supplication they may close the meeting
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words to Mr Herrigel outlining a simple weekly public meeting of prayer, optional song, an address and readings, closing with a supplication; a model of simplicity.

selected.text: establishment of a meeting for the singing of the verses of God, the reading of the Holy Books, the study of the Tablets by the youths of that city, who have sincerely turned their faces to God and became enkindled with the fire of the love of God, abandoned all the conditions that prevent the acquiring of the merciful virtues and the good illumined morals, so that they may love one another and become united in the promulgation of the fragrances of God. The love of God kept them busy from ought else. This establishment is a blessed establishment.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising a meeting of youths for singing verses, reading Holy Books and studying Tablets so that they may love one another and become united.

selected.text: Consider what a bounty He has bestowed. Now this gathering, each from a different place, each soul from a different clime and country - how much difference there was between us, how much strife, how much estrangement! He dawned upon us with His attribute of mercy, gathered us all together, gave us fellowship, united us, and gathered us at one table in such a foreign land. And we are all gathered at this table in utmost love, fellowship, unity and oneness, with no purpose save servitude at His Sacred Threshold, and no desire save love and fellowship.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words to Persian believers in Ramleh recalling how people of different climes, once divided by strife and estrangement, were gathered at one table in love and fellowship.

selected.text: ye beloved of God! Behold how abundant shall be the freshness, tenderness, spirituality, and radiance that are attained when ye assemble in that gathering place of the spirit, occupy yourselves at dawn2 with the remembrance of God, and, after reciting prayers, make mention together of the Most Bountiful Lord in sweet melodies. These melodies shall reach unto the Kingdom of Glory
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: to the offering they have made, it hath been accepted, and as commanded, your honor should receive it and, with wisdom, offer hospitality to the friends of God. Gatherings are in no wise permitted. If several separate meetings be held, this would be more agreeable. When the Most Great Luminary was rising from the horizon of the Land of Mystery, this servant was commanded to write to him who was named Mihdi, whom God caused to dwell in His house after his migration, saying that ye should follow in the footsteps of the Lord of all beings, and associate with the people of the world in the utmost spirit of joy and fragrance, lest alarm and anxiety be aroused among the people and become a cause of disturbance to weak souls
selected.reason: Tablet of Bahá’u’lláh directing that hospitality be offered with wisdom, that separate meetings are preferable to large gatherings, and that the friends associate with all in joy lest alarm be aroused.

selected.text: In truth, these days, which are holidays when souls are joyful and are days of fellowship, love and gathering together, should have some result. There should be some discussions and consultations about beneficial matters, so that they may yield eternal fruits. For example, there should be a general consultation about teaching, a general consultation about charitable works and beneficial matters. In brief, there should be some result; it should not remain without fruit, so that from this joy, delight, attraction, enthusiasm and gladness, traces may become manifest.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words at the Shrine on Naw-Rúz that holy days of fellowship should bear fruit through general consultation about teaching and charitable works; joins celebration to practical care.

selected.text: The great feast that you celebrated on the occasion of the appearance of His Highness, the Bab, likewise the feasts of nineteen days, produced great rejoicing in the hearts of the believers. Whenever the friends and the maidservants of the Merciful gather together, read the Tablets and the words, interchange ideas and deliver eloquent speeches the heavenly blessings descend, the Spiritual Food becomes present, the celestial bounty is unveiled, the confirmations of the Holy Spirit descend uninterruptedly, spiritual development is attained and attractions of heart realized.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing how, when the friends read the Tablets, interchange ideas and speak, spiritual food becomes present and confirmations descend.

selected.text: All over Europe today one hears of meetings and assemblies, and societies of all kinds are formed. There are those interested in commerce, science, and politics, and many others. All these are for material service, their desire being for the progress and enlightenment of the world of matter. But rarely does a breath from the spirit world breathe upon them. They seem unconscious of the Divine Voice, careless concerning the things of God. … But this meeting in Paris is a truly spiritual one. The Divine Breath is poured forth in your midst, the light of the Kingdom is shining in all hearts
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Look ye not upon the fewness of thy numbers, rather, seek ye out hearts that are pure. One consecrated soul is preferable to a thousand other souls. If a small number of people gather lovingly together, with absolute purity and sanctity, with their hearts free of the world, experiencing the emotions of the Kingdom and the powerful magnetic forces of the Divine, and being at one in their happy fellowship, that gathering will exert its influence over all the earth. The nature of that band of people, the words they speak, the deeds they do, will unleash the bestowals of Heaven, and provide a foretaste of eternal bliss.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: this meeting will bear great results, may it be like the meeting of the rain with the earth; may it be like the meeting of the breeze with the garden; may it be like the meeting of the Sun with the mirror -- May great results come from it, may wonderful traces emanate from it amongst humanity. … There are many meetings, one is due to family relations, another because of commercial ends or another meeting may be for political reasons. All are due to one or another purpose, but all such meetings no results are forthcoming, anyway if they do bear results it is only temporary, not lasting. There is the meeting for the sake of God. This causes ideal attractions
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words wishing that a meeting be like the meeting of rain with earth, breeze with garden and sun with mirror, contrasting meetings for family, commerce or politics with the meeting for the sake of God.

selected.text: to you, O ye other handmaids who are enamored of the heavenly fragrances, arrange ye holy gatherings, and found ye Spiritual Assemblies, for these are the basis for spreading the sweet savors of God, exalting His Word, uplifting the lamp of His grace, promulgating His religion and promoting His Teachings, and what bounty is there greater than this? These Spiritual Assemblies are aided by the Spirit of God. Their defender is 'Abdu'l‑Baha. Over them He spreadeth His wings. What bounty is there greater than this? These Spiritual Assemblies are shining lamps and heavenly gardens, from which the fragrances of holiness are diffused over all regions, and the lights of knowledge are shed abroad over all created things. From them the spirit of life streameth in every direction. They, indeed, are the potent sources of the progress of man, at all times and under all conditions

selected.text: God has created Thursday night and Friday for His servants' delight, relieving them during these hours from occupations that might burden them and veil them from their pleasures - each according to what they find delightful: those who glorify through their glorification, those who sanctify through their sanctification, those who unite through their unification, those who magnify through their magnification, those who eat through their eating, those who drink through their drinking, those who beautify through their beautification, those who take pleasure in what God has ordained for them, and those who refine through their refinement - each according to what brings them delight.
selected.reason: Writing of the Báb on Thursday night and Friday as times created for the delight of His servants, each according to what they find delightful; a distinctive scriptural view of sacred time.

selected.text: Throughout the world there are innumerable meetings and assemblages, more or less important according to their measure of contribution to human betterment, yet limited in their purpose and object to material questions and outcomes. They are political, commercial or educational in character; they seek to promote economic advancement, further agricultural purposes, encourage scientific research and assist discoveries; they provide for the establishment of new institutions, plan financial measures and agree upon laws of civic and social control. Such meetings are useful, but their influence and intention do not extend beyond the material welfare and government of mankind -- that is to say, they serve material civilization.

selected.text: written that in New York the devoted handmaid of God, Juliet, the well-assured handmaid of God, Mother Beecher, and the enkindled handmaid of God who is ablaze with God's love, Mrs. Brittingham, as well as Mr. Woodcock and other friends, had gathered for a feast, with thyself and Juliet serving as hosts. How blessed are ye for having rendered such a service and for having organized such a feast! Now, in Montreal, exert thine efforts to continue holding such feasts, as these will conduce to the steadfastness and confirmation of the friends and handmaids of God. Then will the fragrances of the divine rose-garden be shed abroad and the quickening breezes of the Abha Paradise be wafted, causing the participants to be moved with boundless joy

selected.text: What a sweet melody reaches the ears of these yearning ones from all directions - it is the glorification and sanctification of the Forgiving Lord and the song and glad tidings of the Day of Manifestation. It is the anthem of "O Glory of God, the Most Glorious" and the singing of "O Thou Most Exalted." It is the call of unity and the high notes of the nightingales of detachment. Praise and thanksgiving be unto the Glorious Lord who has arranged such a gathering whose music and song is the melody of the Supreme Concourse, whose brilliant lamp is the light of supreme guidance, whose gathering's witness is the Blessed Beauty, whose soul-nurturing wine is the love and affection of the Peerless Beloved, and whose delicious food is the heavenly manna.
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising a gathering whose music is the melody of the Supreme Concourse and whose food is the heavenly manna.

selected.text: Thou hast written concerning the meetings and the gathering-places of the believers of God. Such assemblies and congregations will greatly aid the promotion of the Word, and all the audience, whether friends or not friends, become affected. But when the friends have the intention of entering in these meetings and assemblies, they must first make their purpose pure, disengage the heart from all other reflections, ask the inexhaustible Divine Confirmation and with the utmost devotion and humility set their feet in the gathering-place. Let them not introduce any topic in the meeting except the mentioning of the True One, neither must they confuse that merciful assembly with perplexed outside questions. They must either teach or loose their tongues in propounding argument, either commune or supplicate and pray to God, either read Tablets or give out advices or exhortations
selected.reason: Tablet of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaching that those entering a meeting must first purify their purpose, disengage the heart and enter with devotion and humility, keeping the meeting to the mention of God; the guide’s fullest account of preparation.

selected.text: in the Covenant! Thou hast written to Jinab-i-Manshadi concerning the Feast. This festivity, which is held on a day of the nineteen-day month, was established by His Holiness the Bab, and the Blessed Beauty directed, confirmed, and warmly encouraged the holding of it. It is, therefore, of the utmost importance. You should unquestionably see to it with the greatest care and make its value known, so that it may become solidly established on a permanent basis. Let the beloved of God gather together and associate most lovingly and spiritually and happily with one another, conducting themselves with the greatest courtesy and self-restraint. Let them read the holy verses, as well as essays which are of benefit, and the letters of 'Abdu'l-Baha; encourage and inspire one another to love each and all; chant the prayers with serenity and joy; give eloquent talks; and praise the matchless Lord

selected.text: You must conduct your meetings with great dignity and treat with honor those who come to them. Should there be any strangers, treat them with perfect friendship and love. Your duty is to unite all, in order that no disunion exist, especially among the believers. All must feel perfect at home, and especially, free to ask questions. In fact, you must conduct these meeting that they become sociable and charming. You must always read the Words of Baha'u'llah--from the Ighan. selected.text: Profitless discussions fatigue and weary a person. People who call on me almost every day carry on a stream of profitless, unspiritual talk and I must listen to them with patience. We are commanded to associate with all the people. Today three persons called and they talked for one hour without any definite result. … Manis speech is the revealer of his heart. In whatever world the heart travels, manis conversation will revolve around that center. From his words you can understand in what world he is traveling, whether he is looking upwards to the nether world, whether he is mindful or unaware, whether he is awake or asleep, whether he is alive or dead.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words that profitless, unspiritual talk wearies a person, though He listens with patience because we are commanded to associate with all, and that speech reveals the world in which the heart travels.

Consultation frank and unfettered, is the bedrock of this unique Order. Authority is concentrated in the hands of the elected members of the National Assembly. importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied extract, cited as Ridvan.1996 and given with elisions, states that the flourishing of the community involves the practice of collective worship of God, and that it is therefore essential to the spiritual life of the community that the friends hold regular devotional meetings in local Bahá’í centres, where available, or elsewhere, including the homes of believers. No authority is asserted; keep on merit.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference COC#1973 (4 Feb. 1950 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi) not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied extract, a letter of 4 February 1950 written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi, observes that reading the prayers and meditations of the Writings with friends who are interested in and crave this type of small meeting is often a step towards attracting them to the Faith, and suggests starting such an activity in the recipient’s city. No authority is asserted; keep on merit.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference BA.079 not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied extract, cited as BA.079 and beginning with an elision, states that the assembled representatives of the American believers should not only elect the National Assembly but act as an enlightened, consultative and cooperative body assisting its deliberations, and that the incoming National Assembly should seek the delegates’ advice and sentiments, banish secrecy and aloofness, unfold its plans, hopes and cares, and weigh the delegates’ opinions. No authority is asserted; omit on merit.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference COC#1456 (18 Nov. 1933 from Shoghi Effendi) not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied extract, a letter of Shoghi Effendi dated 18 November 1933 given with elisions, states that the annual Convention is not a body with the functions of an ordinary parliament, that frank and unfettered consultation is the bedrock of the Order, that authority rests with the elected National Assembly while power and initiative are vested in the body of the believers, that the delegates’ twofold functions are to elect and to confer fully and at fixed intervals with the incoming and outgoing National Assemblies, and that only close and constant interaction among these organs can fulfil the Order’s destiny. No authority is asserted; keep on merit.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference COC#1457, LG#60 (25 Dec. 1933 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi) not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied extract, a letter of 25 December 1933 written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi, states that members of both the incoming and outgoing National Spiritual Assemblies should have full right to participate in Convention discussions, that members elected as delegates may also vote, and that this is meant to let them consult more fully and frankly with the delegates, described as one of the primary functions of the Convention. No authority is asserted; omit on merit.
